fixes.explanation: That's the worry. Jeroboam says in his heart, "Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David." (1 Kings 12:26) Notice it's a worry he keeps in his heart. Verse 27 shows where it leads, with him picturing the people's hearts returning to Rehoboam king of Judah.

Actually, it's true. Jeroboam says in his heart, "then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah." (1 Kings 12:27) The text says he thinks they might. It doesn't say anyone plans to, so this is a fear and not a fact.

Golden cherubim did exist, and they stood in Solomon's temple, in the inner sanctuary (1 Kings 6:23, 28; 2 Chronicles 3:13). That's not what Jeroboam makes, though. The text says the king "…made two golden calves…" (1 Kings 12:28) Close on the gold, but a very different shape.

Dan it is. "One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan." (1 Kings 12:29) Two calves, two places. Then verse 30 says, "…this thing became a sin…" and that the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
Shiloh isn't mentioned in this passage, friend. The text says, "One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan." (1 Kings 12:29) Bethel and Dan are the two spots.
Jeroboam doesn't put a calf in Hebron, friend. The text says, "One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan." (1 Kings 12:29) Dan is the answer, and Bethel keeps it company.
Right. Jeroboam "…appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites." (1 Kings 12:31) The detail to catch is that last part. The text is clear that these priests were not Levites.

Elders who once served Solomon aren't mentioned in this passage. The text says Jeroboam "…appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites." (1 Kings 12:31) The detail the text gives is that these priests were not Levites.

True. Jeroboam "…ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah…" (1 Kings 12:32) So his feast is like the one in Judah. The text also says it was held in "a month of his own choosing" (1 Kings 12:33).

It's actually true. The text says Jeroboam "…ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah…" (1 Kings 12:32) So his feast is like the one in Judah, friend. Verse 33 adds that the month was "a month of his own choosing."
No Levites from Judah are named in this scene. The text says Jeroboam "…offered sacrifices on the altar…" (1 Kings 12:32) He's the one named at the altar, and the Levites aren't mentioned there.

The elders of Israel aren't mentioned at this altar. The text says Jeroboam "…offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up…" (1 Kings 12:32) The king himself is the one named, friend.
